name: KPI tile
$status: PROPOSED #203, redesigned #261 (Dave's nomination), Dave's eye owed
$floated: ⛔ THE COMPONENT ITSELF IS FLOATED, NOT RULED. s182-D2 (#182) names it and explicitly declines to rule it — Dave, verbatim, quoted in that ruling: 'might be a partially built trend card with option, I haven't decided yet', and the ruling's own words: 'FLOATED, NOT RULED: the trend-card component itself — never launder into a ruling.' Itinerary row 55 is therefore NOT an ordinary gap a worker may close. This meta is a drawn proposal for Dave's eye; nothing in it is a ruling, and it must not be promoted, gated or registered without his word.
purpose: A dashboard tile that states a metric, how it changed, and the SHAPE of that change: label, value, delta and comparison period, with two optional slots — a sparkline at the Chart-sparkline inline scale, and a hue-free target/progress row. Use it when the reader needs to see how a number moved over time, not merely whether it moved. A KPI tile with no series and no target is a Stat card and should be one.
when: shape = one-measure × value-delta-and-series AND series != none — beats stat-card (roles.json when: "default — label · value · delta · period, no series") whenever a series exists to show; yields to Chart-bullet (when: "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta") when target != none, and to runway-bar (when: "the number is 'money vs what is already scheduled'") when the measure is money-vs-scheduled.

with.$note: s254-D2 item 5 (Dave, #254): the sparkline is a COMPLEMENT of this tile, not a chart-panel in its own right — it is the atom that draws the SHAPE of the change this tile's `answers` second word (change-over-time) claims. Authored one direction only; the reciprocal is DERIVED and printed, never written back (s251-D6).

not-with.$note: The DESK example, kept: reviews/ROLES-REVIEW-2026-09-07-v1.html §01. A KPI tile with no series is a Stat card (s247-D3 / DP-08), so a slot that wanted a status-surface reading is not served by this tile.

$differsFromStatCard: THE BRIEF'S EXPLICIT REQUIREMENT, answered plainly. Stat card (GATED) is a PASSIVE ATOM — label · value · delta · period — and it ALREADY carries full delta semantics: arrow, sign and wording, the R-D5 three-channel treatment. So 'metric + delta' (the itinerary's wording for row 55) was never the gap; only 'spark' was. KPI tile is a MOLECULE that composes two already-approved artefacts and draws nothing new: Stat card's anatomy verbatim, and Chart-sparkline's .spark-inline scale verbatim. THE ONE REAL DIFFERENCE: Stat card states the CHANGE (a signed delta against one prior period); KPI tile states the SHAPE of the change (twelve points of history). Choose Stat card when the reader needs the number and whether it moved; choose KPI tile when the reader needs to see HOW it moved. The sparkline atom anticipated this composition: its own source calls .spark-inline 'the KPI / Stat-card scale' and carries .spark-kpi-slot as 'a SPECIMEN-ONLY wrapper standing in for the Stat-card tile'. Neither parent file was touched.

props.name: target
props.$note: NEW #261. { value, target, pace } drives the optional progress row: a border/subtle track, a standing-ink fill, a one-pixel pace tick at alpha-60, and a caption that spells out every figure the bar draws. NO HUE AT ALL, deliberately: whether 48% against a 60% target is a problem is the reader's judgement, not the tile's, and a hue-free bar cannot be misread by a reader who separates colours poorly.

props.name: state
props.$note: NEW #261 — see stateModel. Drawn, not described: loading is a skeleton with aria-busy and an opacity pulse that prefers-reduced-motion kills; empty renders an em-dash value plus a sentence saying why; error renders an em-dash, a rag/error-ink glyph and a 44px retry control that names what it will load; stale renders the full tile plus a NEUTRAL marker chip. Stale is not amber on purpose (Dave is astigmatic; yellow is a problem hue).

$finding-two-seats: ⛔⛔ THE LIVE TWO-RED QUESTION IS VISIBLE ON THIS ONE TILE, AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED HERE (lane brief: inherit the current binding, flag, do not resolve). The tile paints TWO green/red seats side by side because its two parents bind different ones and BOTH were inherited unchanged. The DELTA ARROW takes rag/success #66CC8D / rag/error #F6604C — the FILL seat, byte-for-byte from the gated Stat-card manifest; on a white card that green measures 1.980:1 (measured #203 with the repo's own _contrast_utils.contrast_ratio). The SPARK STROKE takes rag/success-ink #137F3C / rag/error-ink #DA1A00 — the INK seat that s182-D3 rules for this atom; on a white card that green measures 5.090:1. MEASURED ACROSS ALL FOUR THEMES #203 IN A REAL BROWSER, which CORRECTS the smaller claim first drafted here ('they converge in dark mode'): they converge in MONO DARK ONLY. The spark ink is theme-INVARIANT by ruling (s182-D3, measured #182: zero theme-level series overrides) while the arrow fill FORKS PER THEME, so the two seats disagree in SEVEN OF EIGHT PANES. Computed values read off the DOM — arrow vs spark, ratio against that pane's own surface: mono light #66CC8D 1.98 vs #137F3C 5.09 (arrow UNDER the 3:1 floor); mono dark #66CC8D 8.31 vs #66CC8D 8.31 (the one agreement); legacy light #00847F 4.56 vs #137F3C 5.09; legacy dark #00847F 3.62 vs #66CC8D 8.31; console light #5DAC7B 2.74 vs #137F3C 5.09 (arrow UNDER the floor); console dark #5DAC7B 6.01 vs #66CC8D 8.31; supercharge light #5DAC7B 2.54 vs #137F3C 4.71 (arrow UNDER the floor); supercharge dark #5DAC7B 5.48 vs #66CC8D 7.57. THREE of the four themes put the light-mode arrow under the 3:1 non-text floor, not one. s151-D1 clause 2 ('text AND atoms alike') reads as though it already governs the arrow, and Lane E measured the same leg independently this session; but rebinding a ruled colour seat is Dave's, the arrow-only fill treatment may have been deliberate, and surface-never-swap binds. WHICHEVER WAY IT GOES, Stat card and KPI tile must move TOGETHER — a fix to one that leaves the other is exactly how this seam arrived.

accessibility.role: Each tile is role="group" with an aria-label naming the metric and its period. The loading tile adds aria-busy="true"; the error tile carries role="status" on its message; the target track is role="img" with an aria-label that states the value, the target and the pace.
accessibility.spark: The inline spark is aria-hidden and PASSIVE by design (s184-D1: 'INLINE-44px KPI SPECIMEN STAYS PASSIVE'). The tile's value and delta carry the meaning; the line is ambient. It is therefore not a focus stop and needs no per-point markers.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: Direction is carried three ways — the trend glyph, the sign on the number, and the word 'up'/'down' — never by colour. Flat deltas take the neutral rule glyph and say 'No change'. The spark declares data-trend. The TARGET ROW and the STALE MARKER carry no hue at all. Dave is astigmatic and red/yellow are problem hues, so nothing here leans on hue.
accessibility.targetSize: Interactive parts only: the optional table CTA is 44x44, the retry control is 44px tall, and the whole-tile link's hit area is the tile. The stale chip and the target track are not targets. Enforced BY HAND — no gate reads the target token in a snippet.

antiPatterns: Never ship a KPI tile with an empty spark slot AND no target row — that is a Stat card, and it should be one.

Never let the delta text wear the delta colour. Dark rag/error measures 3.66 as text; the glyph carries the colour at the 3:1 atom floor and the number stays ink (R-D5/R-D6, inherited from Stat card).
Never give the inline spark per-point focus stops or hover markers — a spark is ambient and the markers fight the axis-free idiom (receipted at #182).
Never colour the target row. It is hue-free by design; a red bar for 'behind target' makes the tile pass judgement, which is the reader's job.
Never render the stale marker in amber. Age is carried by the glyph and the sentence — Dave is astigmatic and yellow is a problem hue.
Never render an empty metric as 0. A zero is a measurement; an em-dash plus a sentence is an absence.
Never label the retry control 'Retry'. Name what it will load, so it survives being read out of context.
Never label the table affordance 'View as table'. s182-D2: icon-button form, accessible name only.
Never fix the glyph seat here alone. Stat card and KPI tile bind the same delta seat and must move together.
REVIEW Never promote, gate or register this component without Dave's word — s182-D2 floated it and never ruled it.

stateModel.loading: role=group + aria-busy=true, an sr-only sentence naming the metric, and four skeleton blocks at text/default alpha-08 with a 1.6s opacity pulse that prefers-reduced-motion kills. No spinner, no JS.
stateModel.empty: label + em-dash value at alpha-40 + a sentence saying WHY there is no figure ('The account opened in March'), with the neutral rule glyph. Never a zero — a zero is a measurement.
stateModel.error: label + em-dash value + role=status sentence + a 44px control whose label names what it will load ('Load settlement volume again'), never the bare word 'Retry'. The only coloured mark is the rag/error-ink glyph, whose inner marks take the tile surface.
stateModel.stale: the full, real tile PLUS a neutral marker chip ('Last updated 3 days ago') with the refresh glyph. The number is not dimmed — dimming a real figure to signal age costs contrast and says 'unimportant', which is the wrong word.
stateModel.$note: NEW #261. Replaces the bare string 'simple'. Every state is DRAWN in the snippet, not described.

responsive.board: 12-column bento grid, 16px gap; tiles declare spans the meta legalises (compact/default 3, with-target 4, hero 6)
responsive.breakpoints: at 900px every tile re-spans to 6 and hero to 12; at 560px everything spans 12. Re-spanning, never reflowing — s248-D3, because an edit mode is coming and anything placed in a bento tile must be responsive.
responsive.rows: every row reserves min-height:var(--slot) — the height its own type composite publishes in type.css — so neighbouring tiles align their label, value and delta rows even when one tile has no delta.
responsive.spark: carries NO width of its own (s184-D1, 'responsive to its enclosure by default'); the tile's slot owns the width and the atom fills it.

dimensions.$note: tableCta 44 and retry 44 are the ruled min-hit-area. The stale chip is a 24px NON-interactive marker, so the 24px dial-down floor is not in play — it is not a target. The 200x48 spark viewBox is Chart-sparkline's inline scale, unchanged; only the rendered slot height moves.

groupsWith.$note: RULED s245-D7 (#245). Group 'This month' (knowledge/snippets/Template-dashboard-bento.reference.html: the tpl-group-lead section): FOUR Kpi-tiles answer one question - how did this month go. Uniform in kind (rB C2), so the edge is a SELF-edge: a KPI groups with the other KPIs of its period, never with a chart because it is 'a KPI'. MODULE level (s245-D7 Q7(a)).
